Rashi on Ketubot 10b:10:1.hebrew: דכתיבא באורייתא - ועדיין לא נתקנו כתובות:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:10:1.english: That is written in the Torah - And the marriage contracts had not yet been instituted.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:10:2.hebrew: ומי כתיב קרא - לקרות על שם דבר העתיד:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:10:2.english: And does a verse write - to call [something] by the name of a future matter?

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:10:3.english: This is Seleucia - The name of a city.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:10:4.hebrew: ומי הואי - העיר בנויה בבריאת עולם? דכתיב ״ההולך קדמת אשור״:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:10:4.english: And did it exist? - Was the city built at the creation of the world? For it is written: "that goes toward the east of Asshur."

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:11:1.hebrew: [מטר - ולא מאותיות דריש הכי, אלא לפום סברא]:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:11:1.english: [Matar (rain) - He does not derive this from the letters [of the word], but rather based on logical reasoning.]

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:11:3.english: Refines - It gives delicacy and radiance to the fruit.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:11:4.english: Its ridges - [This refers to the ridges] of the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:11:5.hebrew: רוה נחת גדודיה כאשר ברביבים תמוגגנה - "רוה" — הרי זה משקה ומרוה. "תמוגגנה" — הרי זה מזבל. מעדן וממשיך את הפירות — נפקא מ"צמחה תברך". "תמוגגנה" פירושו בלעז דישטנפי"ר:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:11:5.english: “Watering abundantly… settling its furrows… with showers You make it soft” - “Watering abundantly” — behold, this [means that the rain] irrigates and saturates. “You make it soft” — behold, this [means that it] fertilizes. [That it] refines and causes the fruit to proliferate is derived from “You bless its growth.” “Temogegenah” [means] distemprer in Old French [i.e., to soften].

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:12:1.english: Meziaḥ (moves) - It would enter one's mind [to think that it means] it moves sins.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:12:3.hebrew: מחבב - הוא את ישראל אל אביהם:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:12:3.english: Endears - [The altar] endears Israel to their Father [in Heaven].

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:12:4.hebrew: היינו מזיח היינו מכפר - הי ניהו מזיח, הי ניהו מכפר:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:12:4.english: This is [the same as] moving; this is [the same as] atoning - Which is [the one that] moves, and which is [the one that] atones?

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:12:5.english: It moves decrees - [that are] evil, away from Israel.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:10.hebrew: מבטלות מחשבה רעה - דאגה, לפי שמשמחות את הלב, וצהרים שעת אורה וצהלה היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:10.english: They negate a troubling thought - [Meaning,] worry, because they gladden the heart, and noon is a time of light and joy.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:3.hebrew: מאשרן - מחזיקות כח, כמו "אשרו חמוץ" (ישעיהו א):
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:3.english: Strengthen them - They maintain [one's] strength, like "Strengthen [the] oppressed" (Isaiah 1).

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:4.hebrew: ולא מפנקן - אינן מרבות אסטניסא על הלב, וכלן לשבח:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:4.english: And do not pamper - They do not increase delicacy [astenisa] upon the heart, and all [these effects] are for praise.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:5.hebrew: אל יורה - שום הוראה, לפי שטורדות דעתו כשיכור:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:5.english: He should not issue rulings - any ruling, because [dates] disturb his mind like a drunkard.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:6.hebrew: שחרית וערבית יפות - כללא דמילתא: לאחר אכילה יפות. שחרית — דרכן של בני אדם לאכול בפת שחרית, כדאמר בהמקבל (ב"מ קז:). ערבית — לאחר אכילה:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:6.english: In the morning and evening [they are] good - The general rule of the matter: [dates] are good after a meal. In the morning — it is the way of people [to eat] bread in the morning, as stated in [the chapter] Hamekabel (Bava Metzia 107b). In the evening — [it is] after a meal.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:7.hebrew: במנחה רעות - שהן קודם אכילה, לאחר שינת הצהרים:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:7.english: In the afternoon, [they are] bad - For they [are eaten] before [one's] meal, after the midday sleep.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:8.english: At noon - After the meal, when he ate and was satiated.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:13:9.english: Unparalleled - And [they are] better than [those eaten in] the evening, because during the day one is not prevented from going to the fields, to the privy, whenever he wishes; but at night it is a burden for him.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:1:1.english: Calendering - [It is] to polish (in Old French: lisser), with a glass stone.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:1:2.hebrew: ככיבוס שלהן - שהיו מימיהם יפים לכבס, או סמנין יפים היו להן לכבס. ובכיבוס שלנו אין הבגד מלובן עד שיהיה מגוהץ:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:1:2.english: Like their laundering - For their waters were good for laundering, or they had good cleansing agents for laundering. But with our laundering, the garment is not whitened until it has been calendered.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:1:3.hebrew: מעברא ליה חומרתא - שפשוף האבן מעביר את הדם:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:1:3.english: The stone removes it - The rubbing of the stone removes the blood.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:1:4.hebrew: חומרתא - אבן, כדאמרינן בגיטין (דף סט:) "ונזדהר בחומרתא דנפק מיניה אבן", והיינו הנמצאת באמה מחמת חולי:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:1:4.english: Chumarta - A stone, as we say in Gittin (69b): "And he should be careful with the chumarta from which a stone emerges" — [that is,] a stone found in the urethra due to illness.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:2:1.hebrew: ריחה נודף - מפיה מריחין ריח היין שנכנס לה דרך פתח הפתוח:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:2:1.english: Her scent diffuses - From her mouth one smells the scent of the wine that entered her through an open passage.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:3:1.hebrew: גמרא הוה שמיע ליה - שעשו כן לבנות יבש גלעד, במסכת יבמות (דף ס:):
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:3:1.english: He had heard it as a tradition - That they did so with the daughters of Yabesh-Gilad, in tractate Yevamot (60b).

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:5:1.hebrew: דור קטוע - שאין להם לא דם נדה ולא דם בתולים:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:5:1.english: A truncated generation - For they have neither menstrual blood nor hymenal blood.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:5:2.hebrew: יפין לאשה - דמים יפים למהר לה הריון:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:5:2.english: Beneficial for a woman - [Blood is beneficial] to hasten pregnancy for her.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:6:1.hebrew: נתחייב במקחך - על כרחך תקבל חובה הבאה לך במקחך. לשון "אין חבין לאדם" (לקמן כתובות דף יא.) — דבר שהוא לרעתו קרוי חובה:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:6:1.english: You are obligated in your purchase - Despite yourself, you must accept the liability that comes to you through your purchase. [It is] the language of "one does not confer a benefit on a person" (below, Ketubot 11a) — a thing that is to one's detriment is called a "liability."

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:7:1.english: That their faces were black - Due to hunger.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:7:2.hebrew: צפד עורם - דונש פירש: כמו דבק עורם על עצמם. ומנחם פירש: שחר עורם:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:7:2.english: Their skin shriveled - Dunash explained: [it is] like "their skin clung to their bones." And Menachem explained: their skin turned black.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:8:1.hebrew: בתולה אלמנה וגרושה - בין בתולה שהיא אלמנה, או גרושה, או חלוצה מן האירוסין, וחזרה ונשאת:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:8:1.english: A virgin, a widow, and a divorcée - Both a virgin who is a widow, or a divorcée, or a ḥalutza from betrothal [i.e., before the marriage was consummated], and [who] remarried:

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:8:2.hebrew: כתובתה - של בתולה היא מן השני:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:8:2.english: Her marriage contract - [A virgin's marriage contract is collected] from the second [marriage].

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:8:3.hebrew: מאתים - שהרי בחזקת בתולה היא נשאת לו:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:8:3.english: Two hundred - For she was married to him with the presumptive status of a virgin.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:8:4.hebrew: ויש להם טענת בתולים - אם לא מצאה הב' בתולה, אבדה כל כתובתה, דמקח טעות היא לו:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:8:4.english: And they have a claim of virginity - If the husband did not find her a virgin, she loses her entire marriage contract, for it is a mistaken transaction for him.

Rashi on Ketubot 10b:9:2.hebrew: על שם מנה - שאם נשאת משנתאלמנה, אין לה כתובה אלא מנה:
Rashi on Ketubot 10b:9:2.english: After [the] maneh - For if she remarried after she became a widow, she has no marriage contract [payment] other than a maneh.

Tosafot on Ketubot 10b:10:1.hebrew: אלמנה דכתיבא באורייתא מאי איכא למימר - והא ליכא למימר דתפשוט מהכא דכתובת אלמנה מנה מדאורייתא, דהא מנה לא היה בימי משה, דלא הזכירה תורה אלא ככר. והא דאמרינן בבכורות (דף ה. ושם): משה רבינו נאמן היה ובקי בחשבונות, אלא שמנה של קודש כפול היה — לא שהיה מנה בימי משה, אלא כלומר: כמו שמנה של קודש בימי יחזקאל כפול היה, כך היה ככר של קודש כפול בימי משה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 10b:10:1.english: "[As for] 'widow' that is written in the Torah, what is there to say?" - And one cannot say that [the Gemara] should derive from here that the marriage contract of a widow is a maneh by Torah law, for a maneh did not exist in the days of Moses, as the Torah mentions only a kikar [talent]. And as for what we say in Bekhorot (5a, there): "Moses our teacher was trustworthy and expert in calculations, but the maneh of the sanctuary was double" — [this does] not [mean] that there was a maneh in the days of Moses; rather, it means: Just as the maneh of the sanctuary in the days of Ezekiel was double, so too the kikar of the sanctuary was double in the days of Moses:

Tosafot on Ketubot 10b:10:2.hebrew: ותנא רב יוסף אשור זו סליקא ומי הואי - פי' בקונטרס: ומי הואי בבריאת עולם. ובלא רב יוסף, מאשור וכן מכוש לא מצי למיפרך, דמצינן למימר דאשור וכוש שם המחוז ולא שם העיר, ומימות עולם היה שמם כך. אבל קשה, דמאי מייתי מאשור? דאשור, אע"ג דלא הוה בבריאת עולם, כיון דהוה בימי משה שפיר הוה ליה למכתב; אבל מנה לא היה לו לכתוב, כיון שעדיין לא היה בדורו. ונראה לר"י לפרש: דסליקא בימי משה מי הואי? דקים ליה דסליקא לא היה בימי משה, וסביב סליקא הולך חדקל, ולא אצל אשור שהיה בימי משה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 10b:10:2.english: "And Rav Yosef taught: Ashur is Selika. And did it exist?" - [The text of] Rashi explains: "And did it exist?" — at the creation of the world. And without [the statement of] Rav Yosef, [the Gemara] could not have objected from Ashur, and likewise from Cush, for we could have said that Ashur and Cush are the names of the region and not the name of the city, and from the days of the world's [creation] their name was so. But it is difficult: What is the proof from Ashur? For Ashur, even though it did not exist at the creation of the world, since it existed in the days of Moses, it was proper for him to write it; but [the term] "maneh" he should not have written, since it did not yet exist in his generation. And it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak to explain: "Did Selika exist in the days of Moses?" — for he knew that Selika did not exist in the days of Moses, and the Tigris flows around Selika, and not by Ashur, which existed in the days of Moses:

Tosafot on Ketubot 10b:13:1.hebrew: אמר רב אכל תמרים אל יורה - ואם תאמר: דבפ"ג דכריתות (דף יג: ושם) (אמר רב הונא) אמר רב: הלכה כר' אלעזר, דאינו מחייב על שאר משכרין אלא על היין בלבד. וי"ל: אע"ג דלא מחייב על ביאת מקדש, אסור להורות. וה"נ משמע בס"פ אלו מומין (בכורות מה:), דפסול לעבודה למאן דלא מחייב אשאר משכרין, אף על גב דעבודה לא אחיל, הוא הדין נמי דאל יורה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 10b:13:1.english: Rav said: One who ate dates should not issue [halakhic] rulings - And if you ask: In the third chapter of Keritot (13b, there) Rav [Huna] said that Rav said: The halakha follows Rabbi Elazar, that one is not liable [for entering the Temple] on account of other intoxicants, but only on account of wine alone. And one can answer: Even though one is not liable for entering the Temple [after consuming them], it is forbidden to issue rulings. And so it also implies at the end of [the chapter] "These are the blemishes" (Bekhorot 45b), that one who is not liable for [drinking] other intoxicants is disqualified from the Temple service. Even though [in that case] the service is not profaned, the same applies as well [here], that he should not issue rulings:

Tosafot on Ketubot 10b:8:1.hebrew: בתולה אלמנה גרושה חלוצה - נראה לפרש דלרבותא נקט חלוצה, דסלקא דעתך אמינא: כיון דשומרת יבם לא מיחסרא כניסה לחופה, שהרי יבמה יבא עליה בעל כרחה, וה"א דכנשואה דמיא — קמ"ל:
Tosafot on Ketubot 10b:8:1.english: A virgin, a widow, a divorcée, a ḥalutza - It appears to explain that [the Mishnah] mentioned a ḥalutza to teach an extended point, for you might have thought to say: Since a woman awaiting her yavam [levir] is not lacking entry into the wedding canopy, for her yavam may cohabit with her against her will, one would say that she is considered like a married woman — therefore [the Mishnah] teaches us [that she is not]:
